Person-year table of a restrictive confinement release

Source: R/otpyr.R
otpyr.Rd

Reduces a placement-level release of Ontario's restrictive confinement records (table a01 of the open data, one row per person, fiscal year, pair of regions and alert configuration, with a count of placements) to one row per person and fiscal year, carrying placement volatility (plcvol()), alert complexity (alrtcx()) and the covariates of Ruhela (2026): gender, age group, fiscal year and regional cluster (the regions the person-year's records name, sorted and joined by " + ").

Usage

otpyr(
  x,
  cols = NULL,
  years = NULL,
  ord = "region",
  keep = c("100", "010", "110", "011", "111", "000"),
  base = getOption("crimlab.data", "https://data.crimlab.dev")
)

Arguments

x

A data frame, or the key of a table of the open data service.

cols

The column names: a named character vector with any of year, id, ra, rb, gender, age, mh, sr, sw, np (the placements of the row), overriding the defaults.

years

NULL for every fiscal year in x, or the years to keep.

ord

The order of the records for plcvol().

keep

The alert configurations counted by alrtcx().

base

The data service, for a key (see odtab()).

Value

A data frame of class otpyr, one row per person-year: id, year, n (rows), np (placements), within, across, vm, ac, cx, anyal, gender, age, rc; attributes years, drop, ord.

Details

x is the table, or a key of the open data service read by odtab(). Columns are found by cols, whose defaults are the names the release has always used, matched without regard to case or underscores, so the publisher's end_fiscal_year finds EndFiscalYear. The fiscal years are those in the data; years keeps some of them. Identifiers are reassigned every fiscal year in the release, so the person-year is the unit, never the person.

Rows missing any column used are dropped and counted (attribute drop); an alert flag that is neither yes nor no (nor 1 or 0) is a missing one. Alert complexity counts the six configurations the release shows (keep), as the published analysis does.

References

Ruhela, V. S. (2026). Alert complexity and placement volatility in Ontario restrictive confinement data. Major research paper, Centre for Criminology and Sociolegal Studies, University of Toronto.

Examples

d <- data.frame(
  EndFiscalYear = c(2025, 2025, 2025, 2026, 2026),
  UniqueIndividual_ID = c("a", "a", "b", "a", "c"),
  Region_AtTimeOfPlacement = c("East", "West", "East", "North", "East"),
  Region_MostRecentPlacement = c("East", "West", "East", "East", "East"),
  Gender = "Male", Age_Category = "25 to 49",
  MentalHealth_Alert = c("Yes", "No", "No", "No", "Yes"),
  SuicideRisk_Alert = "No", SuicideWatch_Alert = "No",
  Number_Of_Placements = c(3, 1, 2, 4, 1)
)
otpyr(d)
#> otpyr: 4 person-years, fiscal years 2025-2026 (2)
#>  year py  cx  vm
#>  2025  2 0.5 0.5
#>  2026  2 0.0 0.5
